fair_value_reason: ~30x Oct-2027 NTM adj EPS of ~$22 (25% FY27 $19.77 + 75% FY28 ~$22.9-23.3) and ~19.5-20x NTM EBITDA of ~$5.3B, less ~$5.9B net debt, over ~152.5M diluted shares, give ~$650-680. A small allowance for the larger data-center share (~24% of revenue) under the Texas permit halt brings it to ~$660, about spot and in line with the five-agent mean of $658. The round-1 figure of $668 used a ~31x multiple, before agents took a turn off for the Sep 16 hike.

thesis_triggers.event: $455 is ~23x FY27 consensus EPS of $19.77, the peer and pre-2023 multiple, ~31% below spot and above the $404.51 52-week low. A rates-only de-rating to ~26-28x would stop around $515-555. Reaching $455 would take a real break: a 2027 guide below consensus, a sequential backlog decline, NiSource or large-load programs slipping out of 2027, or a hyperscaler or state-permitting retrenchment. That last one matters more now that Technology & Load Centers is ~24% of revenue.

supervisor_summary: In round 2 the five forecasts converged (fair values $630-677, mean $658, P(>= $663) ~0.52). Each now assumes ~30x Oct-2027 NTM EPS after the Sep 16 Fed hike, so EPS growth of ~16-18% roughly offsets de-rating. The main fact correction is that data centers are ~24% of 2026 revenue, not ~10%: agent_3 caught the round-1 misread. Four agents used the wrong figure to soften their bear cases, so I shade the $400-660 zone down by up to a point. I also found that the widely repeated '-2.5% after Q3-25' reaction is not in the price data (it was +1.1%; 2026 prints were all +7-17%), which earns a slight upward tilt into the ~Oct 29 print. Fair value is ~$660, thesis break $455, and the edge over the index is small.
key_drivers: Record backlog of $53.4B, +49% YoY, with 12-month backlog of $32.3B (+61%). Most of the NiSource program is still excluded (Q2 8-K, ops commentary).

Valuation: ~33.5x FY27 consensus of $19.77, rising with 24 up / 0 down revisions in 30 days. Agents assume ~30x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$22 after the Sep 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, so the price outcome turns more on the multiple than on EPS.

Direct data-center exposure is ~24% of 2026 revenue (corrected from ~10%). The Texas halt on all state data-center approvals (TCEQ report due Oct 19) and any 2027 hyperscaler digestion feed into guidance directly.
Q3 print ~Oct 29 against a raised $4.99 consensus. The last three prints rallied 7-17% on the day.
Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 technical recession at 21% (deep market), and the Fed signals one more 2026 hike.
